notes:
## 0.2.231

owes: four new role tokens an administrator can grant at Settings → Users or `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/roles` — `automation` (the broker page and its `/api/v1/broker` twin, answering `404` to an account without it; setup step 7), `apps` (Settings → Apps and `/api/v1/modules`; setup step 3), `hub` (reachability, the live and restart settings, `/api/v1/settings`, `/api/v1/about`, `/api/v1/restart`, the About hub section; setup step 4) and `supervision` (the every-account feed and weather health views and their `/api/v1` twins); `admin` implies each and is still needed for accounts and roles, snapshots and backups and the secret key; the stored `users.roles` column is already free-form, so no migration, and a hub rolled back reads the new tokens as unknown and ignores them (the `admin` account keeps every right it had).
owes: the broker password is now bound to the host, port and TLS setting it was saved with: a save that changes any of the three without a password in the same submit removes the stored one (state `refused_no_password`, with a new sentence on `/settings/broker`), so an operator who moves the broker enters the password again; `POST /api/v1/broker` behaves the same.
owes: the role labels on Settings → Users change, `Admin` → `Administration` and `Updater` → `Updates` (and their translations), and each role gains a hint; an `admin` account no longer decides alone who can turn apps on, restart the hub or open `/settings/broker`, since an account holding only the matching role now can too.
owes: new endpoints — `GET /mqtt` (the MQTT sync page, every signed-in account while `mqtt.host` is set, `404` while it is off), `GET /api/v1/mqtt` (the same model as JSON, `404` while the broker is off: `connection`, the broker's own `state` only for `automation`, and the caller's own `sensors` with `lastMessageAt`, never a value), `GET /api/v1/broker/test/{id}` and the engine methods `mqtt.status` and `admin.broker.testResult`; a reverse proxy needs nothing new, and a rollback only loses the page and the routes.
owes: `POST /api/v1/broker/test` and the engine's `admin.broker.test` take a new optional `{async: true}` and then answer `{testId}` at once (the default stays synchronous with `{state}`), and `POST /settings/broker/test` now redirects to `/settings/broker?test=<id>` instead of waiting up to 13 s: the test runs as one hub-wide job whose result is kept in memory for 2 minutes, the page refreshes itself with a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` while it runs and, after a save, while the broker is still connecting (up to 8 times); the old `?tested=<state>` address is no longer read; no migration, key or default changes, rollback safe.
owes: the panel footer row *Sync status* now reads *App sync* (and its translations) and its dot is computed from the account's own devices instead of always green, and a new *MQTT sync* row appears under it for every account while the broker is on, so the broker's existence and its connected, connecting or failing state are now visible to accounts without `automation` (its address, user name and certificate still are not); no migration, key or default changes.
owes: nothing beyond the lines above for the two layout changes in this release — the settings and setup pages share one layout (SPEC-150: one 640px left-aligned column, buttons at their content width instead of stretched to 360px, status in a compact card, refusals and results as banners, fields in labelled groups) and the weather pages are wider and tidier (SPEC-149: the board, a city, *Manage places* and Accuracy use a 1280px column with full-width tables, a city's header carries its sensor and a labelled source button, *Manage places* is a list with a row menu, Accuracy lists each city's way to a sensor and dates its collecting sentence, and the sensor page follows find, type, where, label, actions); every route, form field, `hub_state` key and `/api/v1` answer is unchanged (the sensor page also reads one new optional query parameter, `pick`, beside its per-field ones), no migration, rollback safe.
owes: none
